record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: Characterize all commutative and associative binary operations O:[0,1]^2 -> [0,1] with neutral element 1 for which the induced map beta_O on finite subsets of [0,1], defined by beta_O({x1,...,xn})=O(x1,O(x2,...,O(x_{n-1},xn))), is a witness map. In this setting, being a witness map means that beta_O(empty set)=1, beta_O({x})=x, and for every finite A subset [0,1] and every X subset A, the alternating sum over all Z with X subset Z subset A of (-1)^{|X|+|Z|} beta_O(Z) is nonnegative.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $O\colon [0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ be a commutative and associative binary operation with neutral element $1$ (so $O(x,1)=x$ for all $x\in[0,1]$). For a finite subset $A=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\subseteq[0,1]$, define
$$\beta_O(A)=O(x_1,O(x_2,\ldots,O(x_{n-1},x_n)\ldots)),$$
with $\beta_O(\emptyset)=1$ and $\beta_O(\{x\})=x$ (commutativity and associativity make this independent of ordering).

The map $\beta_O$ is called a witness map if, in addition, for every finite set $A\subseteq[0,1]$ and every subset $X\subseteq A$,
$$\sum_{X\subseteq Z\subseteq A}(-1)^{|X|+|Z|}\,\beta_O(Z)\;\ge\;0.$$

Characterize all such operations $O$ for which $\beta_O$ is a witness map.
